I sign on the keycard and the keycard doesn' t show anything useful for contract ABI, so I trust on my own vibecoded wallet WTF if you conflict with a real chain on 32 bit that's a lottery ticket to buy uint32 or int32? https://github.com/ethpandaops/template-devnets/pull/188 That really feels like a keystone bug that they should fix 😄 ChainId is not a 32 bit field. even 64bit would be too small as 256 bit chainIds seem to be getting a thing Going forward new devnets will fit ser don't use a hardware wallet for devnets😂 i have a browser and a throwaway wallet just for devnet shit he's using his potuz.eth wallet for this 😂 I use potuz.eth as a throwaway 🙂 it's a convenience for everyone, just send me to potuz.eth. Also since I use it everywhere I get a chance to trying to trick my friends into making it the default fee recipient on Prysm prysm doesn't take ens as fee recipient yet if you add support for this, I'll set mine for 24h to potuz.eth I don't fully get the tx o.O Dora looks a bit broken on it, but it seems to be signed with the correct chainid I think he had a display issue it was showing him the 32bit truncated version of our chainid but when signing it was the correct one https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/tx/0x130ad7e6d13bb3dee6119ee7b54808cb49b844ed56f2805d79148807a776e2f7 ^ dora is kinda freaking out on that tx too. no traces, no matching receipt, invalid properties or maybe I also misunderstood potuz is fuzzing with his keystone wallet 😂 https://github.com/KeystoneHQ/keystone3-firmware/pull/2284 <@755590043632140352> for your next software release 😄 hmmm that's interesting, how much stake do you have? that may make a difference yes, it's a bug in the Keystone's UI that cuts the chainid at 32bit but the signature is made on the raw hash that is sent https://klipy.com/gifs/yes-nod-46 I do not update hardware wallets, even if they are vulnerable, I will only consider it if they are vulnerable to a contract I may interact look at this guy
